utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are beginning our session with some delay. We've had technical problems. Mr. Registrar, can you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I'm turning towards the Prosecution for the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Counsel. For the Prosecution, Chester Stamp and Ekkehard Withopf, and I would like to use this opportunity to introduce our new case manager, Mrs. Ruth Karper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Defence teams, please, appearances.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Representing General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel; Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel; and Alexis Demirdjian, legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Representing Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Mr. Mulalic, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Chamber would like to greet everybody after the weekend, the representatives of the Prosecution. We also greet the arrival of Mrs. Ruth Karper, who's going to reinforce the Prosecution team and who is going to replace Mrs. Fleming, and who is going to contribute to the smooth proceedings. So Chamber would like to greet this new person on board. The Chamber would also like to greet the Defence teams, as well as the accused and everybody in the courtroom, not to forget the interpreters, who are doing a very important job for everybody. I believe that we have to go into private session because of the application for protective measures. Mr. Withopf, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Mr. President. The Prosecution will apply for protective measures, and for that reason I would suggest to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The positions we have mentioned were positions that you held when the war broke out; that is to say, when JNA and Serbian forces attacked Bosnia and Herzegovina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not receive the interpretation of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My microphone is switched on. I'll repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that the war broke out, the Yugoslav National Army and the Serbian forces attacked Bosnia and Herzegovina, while you were occupying the positions that we already referred to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 6th of April, Bosnia and Herzegovina was recognised by the European Community, by the Republic of Croatia, and the USA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time in Bosnia and Herzegovina legally elected organs at elections in 1990 were in power; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we are in open session, I have to turn off my microphone whenever you answer my questions in order to make sure that your voice isn't heard. After this attack, Bosnia and Herzegovina declared a state of war and introduced a general mobilisation; are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war, in Bugojno municipality there was a Territorial Defence staff, and at the beginning Zdravko Stanisic was its commander. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that, as the commander of the Bugojno Territorial Defence staff, Zdravko Stanisic didn't accept the invitation from the Ministry of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the order from the staff according to which he should subordinate the Municipal Staff to the staff of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. ZH, would it be correct to say that after the beginning of the war most of the Serbian population from Bugojno municipality withdrew with the Serbian army from the town itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, look, the Serbian army wasn't present in the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But most of the Serbian inhabitants left Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of the Serbian inhabitants left Bugojno, and they weren't escorted by the Serbian army because the Serbian army wasn't present in Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. Would it be correct to say that in May in Bugojno an HVO brigade was formed, the Eugen Kvaternik Brigade, and the majority of the Croatian population of Bugojno joined the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, although there were two separate military structures, the Territorial Defence and the Bugojno HVO, as they were faced with the same enemy, attempted in May 1992 to reach an agreement about forming a joint command for the defence of the town. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, the HVO was better organised and the Territorial Defence was being established a little belatedly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, in spite of those attempts, nothing came of this joint command. But in the course of 1992, the Territorial Defence and the HVO carried out combat activities at the lines in the town facing the Serbian forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All those --

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll turn to Defence. I would like to inform Defence counsel that they should turn off their microphone once the question has been put to the witness. Otherwise, we have a problem. Yes, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a pure technical issue. However, since we are in open session and the witness was saying that he was personally present at a certain meeting which has been identified earlier on by my learned colleague, I think this portion should be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Registrar, could you prepare an order to redact the witness's answer that concerns his attendance at this meeting. His answer might make it possible to identify the witness. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm bearing this in mind, but I assume that a number of persons attended the meeting so that the connection with the witness wasn't direct. But my colleague is quite right to point out that even slight -- minor details might reveal the witness's identity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that in July the HVO as a civilian organ of power was formed in Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, that was a period during which de facto and de jure there were two administrative organs in Bugojno, one within the HVO and the other in the BH army. So two directors were appointed to schools and two directors were appointed to companies, and in all the organs of power we had two directors, two persons who were in charge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Witness ZH, that despite the fact that there were parallel bodies of power many individuals and bodies in Bugojno tried to resolve all the problems that might have arose, together, jointly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. ZH, that during 1992 and especially after Donji Vakuf was taken by the Serb forces and after Kupres fell a lot of refugees expelled from that area came into Bugojno? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The increased number of refugees arrived towards the end of 1992 and the beginning of 1993 after the fall of Jajce; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Most of these refugees came without any personal belongings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they arrived in such huge numbers, the situation in the town was further compounded and there were problems with their accommodation and provisions for them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Due to the vicinity of the front line and due to the war, many citizens of Bugojno left the town to go either to the areas which were still not affected by the war or to the third countries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One might say that up to the summer of 1993 a lot of local Croatian population left Bugojno so that in the summer of that year there were only 7.000 local Croats left.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how many Croats were there in the summer of that year, but it is true that a lot of women, children, and elderly people had left. That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Among the refugees who remained in the town, most of them were Bosniak Muslims, so that the demographic picture of the town in mid-1993 was significantly changed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the beginning of war, up to the summer 1993, you were in Bugojno all this time and you didn't go anywhere; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, you are aware of the fact that in order to leave town one had to seek approval by the HVO because the HVO controlled the main roads around Bugojno; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I personally helped some Muslims to obtain those permits, those who wanted to visit their families accommodated in the town of Makarska and in its vicinity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1993, the relationship between the two peoples and the relationship between the HVO and the BiH army was largely affected by the conflicts between the BiH army and the HVO in the territory of Gornji Vakuf and in the Lasva Valley; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, according to your knowledge, both the BiH army command and the HVO command made efforts during the months of May, June, and July to peacefully resolve the situation and to avoid an open conflict. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, on the 17th of July, in the village of Vrbanja, which is some 3 kilometres away from Bugojno towards Gornji Vakuf, there was an incident. Members of the BiH army killed Miroslav Talenta. Milijan Vucak was also killed, and this raised tensions in the town.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. And this day may be taken as the beginning of the large-scale Muslim aggression against Croats in Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that as soon as this fact became known a joint commission was set up, made of four members of the MUP Bosniaks and four members of the MUP who were Croats? They were sent to the spot of the tragedy in order to investigate what had happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that at the moment this joint commission arrived there the HVO attacked Muslim members of the Bosnian-Herzegovinian MUP and killed three out of four of them? Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, you are aware of the fact that these incidents in Vrbanja spread and became a general conflict in the town of Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that during the attack on Vrbanja 54 civilians were killed. They were Bosniak Muslims. 45 of them were arrested and detained in the Aquarium Motel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only learnt that once I was released from the camp. A book was published two years ago depicting those events. While I was detained, I didn't know anything about this incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go back into private session, because my next questions might reveal the identity of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, let's please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. ZH, that at that time in 1993 the BiH army and the HVO as well as the reserve units of the police wore camouflage uniforms in town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is true, but I don't remember. There was no need for me to remember who they were. There were a lot of camouflage uniforms, and the members of these units recognised each other by the insignia on the uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the moment when you were being transferred to the Iskra Stadium, you could see even children wearing camouflage uniforms or parts of camouflage uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you will agree with me that there were even some civilians who had camouflage uniforms and wore them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't agree with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Among the persons who were in the school, you recognised Nijaz Bevrnja; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You could also see that he was the one issuing orders to other soldiers, and based on that you concluded that he had a command responsibility or that he played a important role.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that Nijaz Bevrnja at that time was the commander of a civilian platoon in Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what he was. I know that he was together with Besim Hodzic and that the two of them are responsible for whatever happened in the basement of the Gimnazija building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have testified about spending a month on provisional release. During July, you were not in the prison.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this was not in July. This was in August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. I stand corrected. At first you only spent seven or eight days in the prison, and then for a month you were on provisional release; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stayed in the Gimnazija up to the 8th of October, and then all of those who were still in the Gimnazija building were transferred to the Iskra Stadium; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that throughout all this time the Gimnazija was under the control of the Bugojno MUP, the public security station in Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't believe that it was under the control of the MUP Bugojno. It was under the control of the BiH army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can, please, the Defence indicate the origin and the relevance of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document that we found in the archives of the public security station in Bugojno during our investigation, and this document is directly linked with the building where this witness was detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. ZH, is it correct that the building of the Gimnazija was within the purview of the municipal bodies of the civilian authorities in Bugojno before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. What do you mean within the purview? All the schools before the territory of a municipality are within the purview of their founder, and that is the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In war conditions, the War Presidency of the municipality was authorised to allocate such buildings to certain military bodies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that way, as early as May 1992 the War Presidency of Bugojno made a decision that some parts of the Gimnazija would be given to the public-security station in Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the document that you have in front of you. Are you aware of the fact that in 1993 the chief of the public-security station in Bugojno -- or the civilian police, in other words -- was Mr. Senad Dautovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at this document, can you see that this document bears the heading of the security services centre, public-security station Bugojno? Are you familiar with that heading?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see this for the first time, and I wouldn't be able to say anything about this document because at that time I was already at the stadium. However, it would be logical to say that if the building of the Gimnazija according to this document is given to the MUP, it is only logical that between the 8th and the 14th it was enough time to remove every trace of the crime in order for the Gimnazija to be restored to its original purpose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you will agree with me that this document was issued only four days after the last detainee left the Gimnazija.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not four. Six days later. If this is dated the 14th of October and I left the Gimnazija on the 8th of October, so we are not talking about four days but six days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In my copy, the date is 12.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my copy, the date is 14.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the heading, the date is 12 October, and the deadline for the building to be handed over is the 14th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you are right there. However, I wouldn't be able to say anything about the document. I don't want to comment on this document, because I see it for the first time. I allow that things happened in the way described in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since this document was issued in order to restore the building that is mentioned in the indictment to its original function - this is also the building where the witness was detained - it speaks about direct responsibility of this object in the given period. Therefore, I'm asking for this document to be tendered into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution objects against tendering this document into evidence. The witness has repeatedly -- he has repeatedly said that he has seen this document never, ever before and he can't comment on the document. He can only basically rephrase what is written in this document but nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to mark this document for identification, and we will render our decision tomorrow when we resume the hearing. Mr. Registrar, can we please have a temporary number for this document in B/C/S and for its translation in English.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the B/C/S document will get the exhibit number DH53, marked for identification; and the English translation gets the exhibit number DH53/E, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may proceed, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. ZH, tell us, please, is it true that you personally do not know who was it who decided on the places that would be temporary prisons for members of the HVO and other Croats from Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is true. I don't know who made that decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you also don't know who is it who made the decision on turning the Iskra Stadium into a temporary prison for the detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me tell you. I believe that at that time the master of life and death in Bugojno was Mr. Dzevad Mlaco, the president of the War Presidency of Bugojno, with his associates. Mesud Duvnjak; Kemal Djafic; Enes Handzic; Selmo Cikotic, who was the commander of the military force; Tahir Granic and others. Now, who was it who made such a decision and who was in command of the camps for the Croats from Bugojno, my assumption would be that it was Mr. Dzevad Mlaco and Enes Handzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also don't know personally who was the person who -- or the body who appointed prison wardens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is true that I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spent three days in Duratbegovic Dolac digging the trenches there. Is it correct that Duratbegovic Dolac is in Gornji Vakuf municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what municipality is that. I only know that it is some 10 to 12 kilometres from Bugojno. At that time, this was where the separation line between the BiH army and the HVO was. I don't know the exact distance from Bugojno and that place. I didn't find it important at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. ZH, that you don't know which unit the soldier who received you in Duratbegovic Dolac belonged to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He belonged to a BiH army unit. I don't know which unit it was. I don't know. I didn't ask. I didn't dare ask anything. I wasn't allowed to ask any questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Withopf, could you inform us of our schedule for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution will call the witness which is named on the amended confidential witness schedule which was filed last Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll go back into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As we are now in open session, I would like to adjourn the hearing, and I will see everyone tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning, as we will be having these hearings in the morning this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 2nd day of March, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.44 p.m.,
